images.title: Twelve points, seventeen lines
images.purpose: Show the finished thread design of the concept's example: 12 points on a circle joined by the moves on by 4 and back by 3 until the thread is back at point 1, so the 17 lines can be counted.
images.composition: One large circle with 12 numbered points and 17 coloured lines inside, a heading at the top left and a small colour key on the right.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. HEADING: the text 12 points, 17 lines in bold dark #1F2937 sans-serif (48 px), left edge at x 80, about y 60. CIRCLE: centre (728, 450), radius 290 px, thin dark #2B2B2B outline (4 px), white inside. Exactly 12 points on the circle, each a dark dot (16 px), going clockwise from the top: 1 at (728, 160), 2 at (873, 199), 3 at (979, 305), 4 at (1018, 450), 5 at (979, 595), 6 at (873, 701), 7 at (728, 740), 8 at (583, 701), 9 at (477, 595), 10 at (438, 450), 11 at (477, 305), 12 at (583, 199). Beside each point, outside the circle, its number in bold dark text (34 px), centred at: 1 at (728, 122), 2 at (892, 166), 3 at (1012, 286), 4 at (1056, 450), 5 at (1012, 614), 6 at (892, 734), 7 at (728, 778), 8 at (564, 734), 9 at (444, 614), 10 at (400, 450), 11 at (444, 286), 12 at (564, 166). THREAD LINES, exactly 17 straight lines, each 5 px, drawn between the points. 8 teal #0072B2 lines: 1 to 5 from (728, 160) to (979, 595); 2 to 6 from (873, 199) to (873, 701); 3 to 7 from (979, 305) to (728, 740); 4 to 8 from (1018, 450) to (583, 701); 5 to 9 from (979, 595) to (477, 595); 6 to 10 from (873, 701) to (438, 450); 7 to 11 from (728, 740) to (477, 305); 8 to 12 from (583, 701) to (583, 199). 8 amber #E69F00 lines: 5 to 2 from (979, 595) to (873, 199); 6 to 3 from (873, 701) to (979, 305); 7 to 4 from (728, 740) to (1018, 450); 8 to 5 from (583, 701) to (979, 595); 9 to 6 from (477, 595) to (873, 701); 10 to 7 from (438, 450) to (728, 740); 11 to 8 from (477, 305) to (583, 701); 12 to 9 from (583, 199) to (477, 595). 1 reddish purple #CC79A7 line (the last one, back to point 1): 9 to 1 from (477, 595) to (728, 160). The lines form the path 1, 5, 2, 6, 3, 7, 4, 8, 5, 9, 6, 10, 7, 11, 8, 12, 9, 1. LEGEND on the right: three short line samples (60 px long, 6 px thick) at x 1110 to 1170 with their words (34 px, dark) starting at x 1190: a teal sample at y 300 with the words on by 4; an amber sample at y 370 with the words back by 3; a reddish purple sample at y 440 with the words closing line. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any count of points, numbers or lines that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
a line that is missing or that joins two points other than those listed
a point numbered out of order
images.takeaway: Moving on by 4 and back by 3 from point 1 brings the thread back to point 1 after 17 lines.
images.description: A circle with 12 numbered points joined by 17 lines in the path 1, 5, 2, 6, 3, 7, 4, 8, 5, 9, 6, 10, 7, 11, 8, 12, 9, 1, drawn in teal, amber and one reddish purple closing line.
images.context: Concept image for Joining Points on a Circle. It shows the concept's own 12-point circle and not a figure from your maths book.
images.teaching_notes: Trace the path with a finger and count the lines out loud. The slip to watch is stopping at point 9 and not drawing the last line back to point 1.

image_decisions.why: The 12 points and the 17 coloured lines are the mathematics: the child traces the path and counts the lines in the picture.
